doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Sitting in with Dexter Gordon on Stella by Starlight
summary: Dexter tests him with Stella in A and stops mid-chorus; the rhythm section guides him, and Dexter then asks him to cover a gig in Aarhus.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: played with Bill Evans, recorded with Dexter, and he’s still one of the best drummers I’ve ever heard. So I kind of stumbled into this scene by having the nerve to go up and ask Dexter if I’d get to sit in with him.
Did he like, put you through your paces sort of?
And tell me about that again.
Well I asked him if I could sit in and he said, “well have you got any chops?”
He said do you have any chops?

Yeah. Meaning can I get around the horn. And I said well there are some days I do, some days I don’t. And he was pretty bleary. He’d been drinking pretty hard. So he said, you know, “Stella By Starlight.” And I said, “yeah.” And he said, “in A?” Which puts me in F sharp. And I wasn’t about to let this go, so I said, “sure.” And so we went on stage and Dexter started out “Stella by Starlight” and playing a long, long chorus. I mean, many choruses. He quit in the middle of a chorus and went [motions]. You son of a bitch.
Especially to stop in the middle of a chorus.
Absolutely. He wanted to know if I knew where I was.

Usually it’s in B flat, so it was kind of a half step. And so he played a brilliant rhythm solo. But I was also doing the ugly fan thing — I was standing on stage saying wow, this is Dexter Gordon. I have all his records. But the rhythm section was great. It was Neils Henning was playing bass, and Kenny Drew was playing piano. And they knew what Dexter was doing. And Kenny Drew just kind of rolled his eyes. And he walked me through it. The chord changes — every change was like riding on rails [claps]. There was no surprises, everything was just nice, nice, nice, and it was a delight. An absolute delight. Then Dexter caught me the next day, and I don’t know how he found my phone number because I was staying in a house that a Danish woman was — she would rent rooms. And so he was very nice and he said, “can you cover for me? I have a gig in Aarhus that I have to back out of. Can you do it?” And I said, “sure, I’d love to.” And he said, “good, ‘cause I told them you could.”
